svg.text: HOW TO MAKE IT AND HOW IT FITS

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Buy a threaded 1 1/8 in steel fork with a separate forged crown (the

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: roadster type), steerer at least 250 mm long.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Saw both legs off flush with the underside of the crown; file flat.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Drill two 9 mm holes up through the crown, 32 mm either side of the

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: steerer, on the line of the legs. Use the drop arm as the template.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Cut the steerer to suit the headset stack (about 245 mm above the

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: crown race seat) and fit a tall quill stem (about 350 mm).

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Fit: the crown sits under the lower yoke; the drop arm bolts under it.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Check: the steerer turns freely in the head tube once the headset is
